headline: China reportedly allows ByteDance and Tencent to import 10,000 H200 chips each
summary: The move, reported by the Financial Times, eases US restrictions and aims to boost local companies in training cutting-edge AI models, with other firms potentially receiving similar shipments.
details: ByteDance and Tencent have reportedly received 10,000 NVIDIA H200 chips each over the past few weeks. China is said to be easing restrictions to help these local companies train advanced AI models, allowing them to better compete with American counterparts.

The US government previously banned H200 sales to China due to concerns over military technology development. NVIDIA was only allowed to sell processors to approved Chinese customers, with Reuters reporting China agreed to import hundreds of thousands of H200 chips in January, and the US permitting 10 Chinese firms, including ByteDance and Tencent, to purchase them in May.

These processor shipments have now reportedly begun making their way to the approved firms. While ByteDance and Tencent are allowed to buy up to 100,000 chips each, China reportedly wants most of them kept out of the mainland to support its domestic chip industry.

Authorities have reportedly instructed companies to ship their processor orders to Hong Kong instead, despite not having data centers there. This strategy aligns with China's booming domestic chip industry, as local companies develop their own AI chips to reduce reliance on foreign products amid US export controls.

headline: Apple services like Find My & iCloud were down for users, now confirmed fixed.
summary: Apple's System Status page confirmed issues with core services like Find My and iCloud, affecting both consumers and developers. The outage has since been resolved.
details: Apple's core services, including Find My and iCloud, experienced an outage affecting numerous users and developers. The disruption was officially confirmed on Apple's System Status page, detailing the widespread impact.

Users reported difficulties accessing various functionalities tied to these services. While the downtime caused inconvenience, Apple has since updated its status page to confirm that all affected services are now fully operational and restored.
